variant.label: Low-bar back squat, 150 kg · contact-v2 experiment

model.name: Catelli v4 marker-enabled full-body squat model (Rajagopal/Lai lineage), derived copy
transformations: loaded the byte-identical marker-enabled Catelli v4 model
set appliesForce=false on every Force in the ForceSet (80 muscles, 17 coordinate actuators) so inverse dynamics sees gravity and external loads only

added rigid body 'barbell' (150 kg; Ixx=99.269, Iyy=99.269, Izz=3.2926 kg*m^2 about its COM, bar axis along z) welded to the torso frame at (np.float64(-0.09783386860690368), np.float64(0.355), np.float64(0.0)) m (low-bar)
contact-v2: exact 75 mm analytical palm station closure, continued from the prior 45 mm contact-v2 arm posture; no surface deformation; existing arm coordinate bounds retained
contact-v2: fourth arm constraint sets wrist-to-shaft perpendicular distance to 74 mm, retaining exact palm XYZ closure and all existing coordinate limits
contact-v2 fitted torso weld: [-0.105, 0.355, 0.0] -> [-0.09783386860690368, 0.355, 0.0] m; unchanged source model
model.license_note: SimTK project page records an MIT use agreement; the derived model is generated locally and not redistributed.

assumptions: Kinematics are authored: knee flexion, trunk lean, and tempo follow smooth prescribed profiles; hip and ankle angles are solved so that both feet stay flat and the system centre of mass stays over a fixed midfoot point.
The motion is sagittal and bilaterally symmetric; stance width, toe-out, and left/right differences are not modelled in this variant.
The barbell (150 kg) is a rigid body welded to the torso at the low-bar position, so it cannot roll or slide; hand forces are therefore not resolved.
Arm posture is solved once so the palms sit on the bar and is held fixed relative to the torso.
Ground reaction is derived from the model's own momentum balance (Newton-Euler) and split 50/50 between the feet; the centre of pressure and vertical free moment follow from that balance.
Segment masses and inertias are the generic Catelli/Rajagopal values for a 75 kg lifter; no subject scaling was applied.
Muscles and coordinate actuators were disabled; results are net joint moments, not muscle or joint-contact forces.

Experimental contact-v2 authoring: rigid bar placement is fitted to the unchanged calibrated human surface; palm station contact is an exact IK constraint. All coordinate, balance, bar-load, ground-reaction and net-moment series are recomputed with OpenSim. Surface shape is not a measured anatomical constraint.
claims_boundary: Simulated lift: the kinematics are authored and the external forces are model-derived, not measured. Net joint moments describe this simulation only. No muscle force, joint-contact force, spinal load, coaching, or injury-risk claim is made.

frames.axes: OpenSim ground frame: x forward (toes), y up, z to the lifter's right; body meshes and transforms share this convention

sign_notes.pelvis_tilt: positive = posterior tilt; negative = anterior tilt

bar.force_note: force the lifter must apply to the bar: m_bar * (a_bar - g); equal and opposite to the load on the lifter

ground_reaction.method: Newton-Euler balance of all model bodies incl. barbell from finite-differenced momenta at the sampled rate
ground_reaction.split_assumption: bilaterally symmetric: each foot receives half the total force at the shared centre-of-pressure x under its own midline

inverse_dynamics.method: opensim.InverseDynamicsSolver with finite-differenced speeds/accelerations; ground wrench applied through station/frame Jacobian transposes under each calcaneus

residuals.meaning: Generalized forces left on the six pelvis-to-ground mobilities; near zero means the kinematics, inertia, and applied loads are mutually consistent.

path_screen.note: Pass permits kinematics and net moments only; muscle, static-optimization, and joint-reaction outputs remain out of scope for this bundle.

contact_authoring.arm_seed_strategy: Fixed prior contact-v2 arm pose; seven-station continuation from 45 to 75 mm; low-bar fourth residual continued to 74 mm wrist-to-shaft radial distance; bounded updates
contact_authoring.geometry_scope: Fixed human surface, torso-influenced triangles at the solved arm posture. This is rigid authoring geometry, not compliant tissue or a measured support location.

serialized_contact_check.scope: All serialized analytical frames; exact triangle-to-shaft distance on torso-influenced surface. Browser hand overrides, mesh self-collisions, and visual acceptance are separate checks.
